transcript:
Craig Mychajluk
Vice President of Finance and Investor Relations, Alliance Advisors IR
Thank you, and good morning, everyone. We appreciate your time and interest in Allient. On the call today are Dick Warzala, our Chairman, President, and CEO, and Jim Michaud, our Chief Financial Officer. Dick and Jim will review our Q4 and full year 2025 results, provide a strategic and operational update, and share our outlook. We will open the line for questions. The earnings release and slide presentation are available on our website at allient.com. If you are following along, please turn to slide 2 for the safe harbor statement. Forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those indicated. These risks and factors are outlined in our SEC filings and the earnings release.
We will also discuss certain non-GAAP measures useful in evaluating performance. These measures should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for GAAP results. Reconciliations of non-GAAP to GAAP measures are provided in the tables accompanying the earnings release and slides. Please turn to slide 3. I now turn the call over to Dick.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Craig. Welcome everyone. We entered 2025 with clear priorities: expanding structural margins, strengthening the balance sheet, and positioning the portfolio around durable secular growth drivers. As the year closes, we made measurable progress on all three. Q4 highlights include improving industrial demand, disciplined execution, and structural margin expansion driven by our Simplify to Accelerate NOW program. This performance reflects higher volumes, operating leverage, improved mix, and sustained cost discipline, translating into stronger profitability. Broad participation across industrial verticals reinforced diversification and durability of results.
A significant automation destocking is largely behind us, and ordering patterns are returning to normalized levels. Demand for power quality solutions supporting data center infrastructure remains strong. Vehicle performance exceeded expectations due to commercial auto production timing. Medical remained steady, and aerospace and defense reflected normal program timing dynamics. Q4 results showed broad participation across the portfolio. Margin expansion was not solely volume-driven.
Margin improvement reflected better mix, improved cost structure, and continued execution under Simplify to Accelerate NOW. Operational work from prior years is now embedded in the model. For the full year, 2025 focused on strengthening the company foundation: reducing complexity, improving throughput, and strengthening margins sustainably. Structural savings of $6–7 million were targeted, with meaningful progress realized through footprint optimization and resource focus.
Product development was accelerated by streamlining processes and reducing time to market. Lean manufacturing improved standard work and reduced non-value-added time. The Dothan facility transitioned to advanced fabrication, with assembly work moved to complementary sites. This initiative is expected to reduce costs and complexity across North America. Record gross margins were achieved, and operating income grew ahead of revenue.
We generated record operating cash flow. We reduced net debt significantly, bringing leverage down to levels that gives us real financial flexibility. The balance sheet today looks very different than it did a year ago, and that matters because it allows us to invest in organic growth, support new program launches, and pursue disciplined capital allocation opportunities from a position of strength. With that, let me turn it over to Jim for a more in-depth review of the financials.
Jim Michaud
CFO, Allient Inc
Record operating cash flow was generated. Net debt was reduced significantly, providing financial flexibility. The balance sheet allows investment in organic growth, support for new programs, and disciplined capital allocation. I now turn the call to Jim for an in-depth review of the financials.
Demand for power quality solutions supporting data center infrastructure remained strong. Vehicle revenue increased 35% due to increased commercial automotive shipments tied to a transitioning model program. Construction markets improved, and powersports conditions stabilized. Medical revenue increased 9%, supported by steady demand for surgical instruments and precise motion applications. Aerospace and defense declined 5%, reflecting the lumpy nature of shipments and the previously announced M10 Booker tank program cancellation. Underlying defense program activity remains solid. Distribution channel sales increased 11%, a smaller component of total revenue. Turning to slide 6.
This slide shows revenue composition over the trailing twelve months, year-over-year changes, and key drivers. Industrial remains our largest vertical, anchored by higher-value applications. Power quality for data centers, motion solutions tied to automation, and applications aligned with electrification are where engineering focus and capital have been directed. Aerospace and Defense remains a meaningful and growing contributor. While quarterly shipments can be lumpy, underlying program activity and pipeline remain solid, providing longer cycle visibility. Medical remains steady. Surgical applications continue to be reliable contributors, and precision motion capabilities position us well in this space.
Vehicle is now a smaller percentage of the mix than previously, partly market-driven and partly strategic. We have intentionally shifted from lower-margin programs toward higher-value applications across the portfolio. Today’s mix is more margin accretive and better aligned with durable secular growth drivers. On slide 7, gross margin expanded 90 basis points year-over-year to 32.4%, driven by higher volumes, favorable mix, and operational efficiencies from Simplify to Accelerate NOW. Sequentially, gross margin moderated due to a higher proportion of vehicle revenue, which carries lower relative margins.
For the full year, gross margin expanded 150 basis points to a record 32.8%. Slide 8 highlights drivers behind margin and operating income expansion. The Simplify to Accelerate NOW program was designed to structurally reduce complexity, improve throughput, and strengthen margins. Operating performance reflects this work. Structural savings from 2024 and 2025 are embedded in the business, showing up in leverage and operating income expansion. Realignment costs relate primarily to the Dolphin transition, which has been successful operationally and financially.
Enhanced manufacturing focus and early savings elements are being realized. Combined with improved volume and mix, leverage impact is clear. Expense discipline improved at the operating level. Higher volumes were captured while controlling SG&A, allowing operating income to grow faster than revenue. Q4 operating income increased 76% to $11.4 million (7.9% of revenue). Full-year operating income increased 46% to $44 million (7.9% of revenue). Slide 9 illustrates how structural margin expansion and disciplined execution translated into bottom-line growth. Net income for the quarter more than doubled to $6.4 million ($0.38 per diluted share).
Adjusted net income was $9.3 million ($0.55 per share). Adjusted EBITDA was $19 million (13.3% of revenue), up 170 basis points. Full-year net income was $22 million ($1.32 per diluted share). Adjusted EBITDA was $76.9 million (13.9% of revenue), representing a 210 basis point expansion year-over-year. Full-year effective tax rate was 23.3%. For 2026, expected tax rate is 21–23%. Slide 10 reflects execution against three financial priorities: improving working capital and inventory efficiency, reducing structural costs, and strengthening the balance sheet.
Cash generation reached record operating cash flow of $56.7 million, up 35% year-over-year, reflecting improved profitability and working capital management. Inventory discipline was a major focus in 2025. Automation normalization and rare earth considerations were navigated while improving inventory turns to 3.2 times versus 2.7 at end of 2024. Planning processes were tightened, production aligned with demand, and excess inventory reduced while maintaining strong customer service levels. Receivables day sales outstanding improved to 57 days versus 60 last year, reflecting better collections, stronger billing discipline, and improved customer mix.
Combined inventory turns improvement with DSO reduction demonstrates a structurally better working capital profile. Capital expenditures in 2025 were $7 million, focused on customer programs and productivity initiatives. For 2026, CapEx is expected at $10–12 million, supporting customer programs and growth initiatives. Slide 10 highlights execution: working capital improvement achieved, structural cost reductions realized, and debt re-reduction accomplished. Total debt declined to $180.4 million.
Net debt declined to $139.7 million, a $48.4 million reduction year-over-year. Leverage ratio improved to 1.82x from 3.01 at end of 2024. Bank-defined leverage ratio ended at 2.34, comfortably within covenant levels. Stronger earnings, improved cash conversion, and disciplined CapEx enabled material deleveraging. Benefits include lower financial risk and reduced interest burden, and increased flexibility to invest in organic growth, support new programs, and pursue disciplined capital deployment. Slides 10 and 11 together illustrate operational improvements translating into cash, deleveraging, and flexibility.
That completes the financial overview for Q4. Please advance to Slide 12. I will now turn the call back over to Dick.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Jim. As we moved through Q4, order trends improved. Automation demand is stabilizing, power quality for data center infrastructure remains strong, and our aerospace and defense pipeline continues to provide long-term cycle visibility. Orders were up sequentially and year-over-year, with a book-to-bill ratio slightly above 1. Backlog ended the year at approximately $233 million, with most expected to convert within 3 to 9 months, consistent with historical patterns. This visibility supports a constructive start to 2026. We are positioned to build on momentum while remaining realistic, as the macro environment is uneven across certain end markets.26, we believe we are positioned to build on that momentum. At the same time, we remain realistic. The macro environment is still uneven across certain end markets.
Customer capital spending can move in phases. Policy and tariff considerations remain part of the broader landscape, and we continue to monitor developments closely. We will adjust as needed. Regarding recent Supreme Court rulings and trade policy discussions, we continue to evaluate potential implications. Over the past several years, we have diversified our supply base, localized sourcing where appropriate, and managed tariff exposure through pricing and operational adjustments. We remain disciplined in evaluating these developments. What gives us confidence is what we control: our cost structure, which is structurally stronger than a few years ago, and working capital discipline demonstrated in 2025.
We control capital allocation and strengthened the balance sheet meaningfully over the past year. We continue to align the portfolio around higher-value motion controls and power solutions, serving durable secular drivers of electrification, automation, energy efficiency, increased defense spending, and digital infrastructure. These drivers are long-term shifts in how energy is generated and used, systems are automated, and infrastructure is built. Allient technologies are directly aligned with these transitions. We exit 2025 with improved margins, stronger cash flow, and a materially stronger balance sheet, providing flexibility and resilience and positioning us to execute through varying market conditions. We believe we will enter 2026 from a position of strength.
We have an excellent opportunity to leverage the foundation built through our Simplify to Accelerate NOW initiatives, simplify the organization, drive out cost, and accelerate growth well into the future. Operator, please open the line for questions.
Operator
We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star, then one on a touch-tone phone. For speakerphone users, pick up your handset before pressing the keys. To withdraw a question, press star then two. Our first question comes from Tomohiko Sano with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
Hi, good morning, everyone.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Good morning, Tomo.
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
Thank you for taking my questions. While the cyclical macro recovery, such as improving ISM, is expected, Allient has clearly driven structural growth and margin improvement through initiatives like Simplify to Accelerate NOW. Looking ahead to 2026, which do you see as the bigger contributor to growth and margin expansion: external tailwinds or your own initiatives, such as self-help measures? Any additional color on 2026, please.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Okay. If I understand correctly, you are asking which secular drivers we expect to generate the largest growth opportunities for 2026. Is that correct?
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
I want more insight into the cyclical recovery versus the 2026 secular themes.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Tomo, I’m having a hard time picking up some of the comments—your line is breaking up.
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
I meant, could you discuss 2026 revenue growth driven by cyclical recovery versus structural items? I also want some color on the margin side. Thank you.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Okay, I understand now. As we reposition the business, we see longer-term drivers continuing. Data center infrastructure remains a key opportunity. On the energy side, some companies are generating power independently, which does not affect us.
We play a significant role in ensuring power is delivered efficiently and effectively as data centers expand. This opportunity continues into 2026 and beyond, based on infrastructure and capital projects, subject to prime contractors and developers’ timing. Aerospace and defense, particularly defense, is influenced by many factors.
The ongoing conflict in Iran may impact our business, immediately or long-term—it is too soon to call. Other active programs, including defense applications like drones and missile defense, continue to see our participation and are expected to persist.
North American-based manufacturing and design engineering provides us an advantage for defense products. Medical remains a growth area, particularly with AI and advanced diagnostic tools. Key areas where we have long-term involvement continue to expand.
Industrial automation and robotics, including humanoids, continue to be areas of participation and growth. Germany’s industrial markets remain soft, with no projected growth for 2026. We will monitor developments, but that is the current forecast.
We saw some signs that the market might improve, but the latest information suggests otherwise. Our diversification across multiple markets provides balance. The industrial sector is expected to continue growing due to automation and data center infrastructure. Defense growth is also anticipated, influenced by cycle timing, as Jim mentioned.
The government canceled the M10 Booker program, reflecting a realignment of priorities on the battlefield. Margins are influenced significantly by product mix. Our focus remains on investing in markets with margins above our average, and capital spending will align with this strategy. This disciplined approach positions us well for the year.
Our book-to-bill ratio is improving, which we monitor closely to confirm that opportunities are converting into shipments. This demonstrates that our pipeline is being realized effectively. I hope this answers your questions; if not, I am happy to provide further clarification.
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
Thank you. Very helpful. A follow-up on capital allocation: congratulations on improved leverage and strong cash flow. How do you plan to prioritize capital allocation for 2026 among organic growth, investments, M&A, and shareholder returns?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Going into 2026, our pipeline of opportunities is strong. Investments will focus on areas under our control and immediate opportunities that require funding to realize. This will represent the majority of our capital allocation. We are also monitoring potential acquisition opportunities and are positioned to act if the right opportunities arise.
Regarding Simplify to Accelerate NOW, the initiative is ongoing. Several initiatives were successfully executed, but some actions carried into 2026. We will continue to drive cost reductions and efficiency improvements across our infrastructure and footprint. This is a continuing process.
This is not a short-term effort. There remain additional opportunities in 2026 to improve our cost base. We will actively pursue these initiatives to enhance efficiency and drive value.
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
Thank you, very helpful. That’s all from me.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Tomo.
Operator
The next question comes from Greg Palm with Craig-Hallum. Please go ahead.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Thanks. Morning, everybody. Congrats on a strong finish to 2025.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Greg.
David Brown
Equity Research Analyst, Robert W. Baird & Co.
Appreciate it, Greg.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
I don’t remember the last time you grew revenues sequentially from Q3 to Q4. Maybe it happened once or twice. Was this due to growth in commercial vehicles, or were there other factors? Also, what trends have you seen so far in Q1?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Great question. Q4 is always subject to unknowns. Some demand was pent-up, and supply chain factors caused irregularities in normal cyclical patterns. We experienced a few pull-ins, which elevated Q4 sales. The commercial vehicle side contributed, but other areas also had minor surprises. Some demand shifted, which may reduce Q1 activity, but these are expected offsets.
You know, that was a one-time surge based upon some demand that was sitting out there, and we see it, you know, returning to normal. In a couple other areas, there were a few that surprises, I'll call them, and I won't mention in detail what they were. They were, you know, pulling in product, then as we turned the year, we saw that that was reflected in a little bit lower demand in Q1. There were some offsets there that, you know, we'll be addressing and see as it's still early, of course, but see how that lands.
Overall, three drivers affected Q4: a one-time surge returning to normal and two adjustments after pulled-in demand. Nothing seen will affect annual run rates; it was an unusual quarter.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Across your markets, what is the current demand trend? Any changes or potential risks and opportunities over the past week?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Order inputs are strong, showing continued improvement through the year. We monitor this closely as it indicates future shipments. Encouragingly, the trend appears to be continuing.
Recently, defense product consumption exceeded expectations, indicating a stockpile was being drawn down. Shipments are now resuming, particularly for replenishment of defense-related products. The exact impact is uncertain, but we anticipate seeing results soon.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
You mentioned drones as an opportunity. Can you share any traction or emerging opportunities there?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
We are well-regarded for high-performance solutions and custom engineering. Activity in the drone market has accelerated, including prototyping and quoting. Opportunities are expanding into Class 1/Group 1 devices. This area is a key growth opportunity, and we know how to scale production in volume.
We benefit from maintaining automotive as a single-digit percentage of our business. This allows us to produce higher-volume solutions cost-competitively using automation. I see this as a strong opportunity to redeploy the know-how we have developed over the years into new growth areas.
While pricing and margins may differ from our higher-performance custom-engineered products, volume provides incremental margin contributions. The shift to North America has increased inquiries. Our technology base—electronics, controls, motors, lightweighting, and composites—positions us to expand in these areas, and we are excited about the opportunity.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Last question: you announced a facility expansion for data center work last year. What is the status? Will you have adequate capacity to capitalize on growth opportunities?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
The expansion is progressing well and is expected to be fully operational by late Q2 or early Q3. Timing couldn’t be better. This proactive increase in footprint and capabilities positions us to meet growing market demand, with significant volume increases expected later in the year.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Perfect. Appreciate all the color. Thanks.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Greg.
Operator
The next question comes from Max Michaelis with Lake Street Capital Markets. Please go ahead.
Max Michaelis
Equity Research Associate Analyst, Lake Street Capital Markets
Thanks. Regarding the data center opportunity, based on your prepared remarks and Q&A, can we expect acceleration in growth in 2026 compared to 2025?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Yes. Opportunities are strong. The facility expansion at our main site, nearing completion, is critical to handling increased demand. Last year saw some accelerated deliveries. Order input rates are variable, so growth will not be a smooth incremental trend.
Expect substantial jumps in Q3 and Q4 as orders and shipments ramp. The trajectory will not be linear.
Max Michaelis
Equity Research Associate Analyst, Lake Street Capital Markets
Is growth driven primarily by new customer wins or expanding wallet share with existing customers?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
The market itself is expanding. Our capabilities position us competitively, driving growth. Past acquisitions, including a Wisconsin facility and manufacturing footprint in Mexico, have accelerated our ability to meet demand and support market expansion.
We are leveraging our production capabilities, facility expansions, and technology to strengthen our competitive edge. Our products are recognized as high-performing and cost-effective.
Max Michaelis
Equity Research Associate Analyst, Lake Street Capital Markets
With the M10 Booker program ending, are there other programs you can discuss for future direction?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
I prefer not to share specifics. The M10 Booker program was a multi-year effort. Battlefield priorities are shifting toward smaller, agile, autonomous vehicles. We are positioned well in these emerging areas.
Through acquisitions, we offer fully integrated solutions, including electrification, actuation, motors, controls, drives, IO, and lightweight composites. Composites improve strength, EMI protection, and efficiency in electric and hybrid vehicles, extending battery life.
We are uniquely positioned to offer these solutions to prime contractors. The Department of Defense is emphasizing accelerated development. Leveraging products already used in other markets gives us a competitive advantage, particularly in vehicle applications where we are strong.
COTS (commercial off-the-shelf) products are critical. We can modify them for ruggedness, environmental factors, lighter weight, or higher performance. Investments have been made, and while returns are pending, we are confident in our positioning for the future.
Max Michaelis
Equity Research Associate Analyst, Lake Street Capital Markets
Awesome. Thanks.
Jim Michaud
CFO, Allient Inc
If you have a question, please press star then 1. Our next question comes from Ted Jackson with Northland Securities. Please go ahead.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
Thanks very much. You guys sound so optimistic—it’s infectious.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Ted.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
I have a couple of questions. Dick, regarding the domestication of work: there are two main areas—manufacturing and supply chain. Manufacturing seems straightforward. For supply chain, is there work required to ensure NDAA compliance by January?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Good question. There’s always work to be done, particularly with rare earth minerals and materials in higher-performing products. We have the capacity to produce in North America, with about 1.2 million square feet of manufacturing space. Facility rationalization over the past years gives us a redeployable footprint, which is to our advantage.
We have space for quick ramp-ups for certain initiatives. Supply chain remains a challenge; we are actively working on it. While not fully solved, we are addressing government policies and other external factors.
We are minimizing impacts and solidifying supply chain sources. Ramp-up hasn’t been as fast as desired, and alignment between government objectives and reality will take time. We are proactively regionalizing our supply chain.
These efforts are independent of tariffs or duties—they were logical business decisions. We remain prepared but cannot control all external factors. Jim, anything to add?
Jim Michaud
CFO, Allient Inc
Ted, federal investments in US companies are ongoing. Supply chain compliance, including rare earths, will evolve and likely won’t be fully resolved by January 1.
We have teams working diligently with suppliers to lay the foundation for partnerships aligned with government investments.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
Regarding magnets, everyone has that challenge. Does the government understand practical limitations? Are you in dialogue with them?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Yes. We are in close contact with government officials and identified sources being supported. Reality and desire must align. We remain fully engaged and committed.
It’s a continuous effort to work all angles while staying close to key government activities.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
Beyond magnets, are there other critical components that require resourcing for compliance?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Yes, but they are less complicated. Costs are a factor. Some electronic components face supply shortages due to demand in other sectors. For motors, alternatives exist for laminated steel and bearings, though they may be costlier.
Magnets are unique and deserve attention. Other components are impacted by external factors but are manageable.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
This will remain a discussion topic each quarter. On commercial vehicles in Q4, can you quantify the one-time impact to help frame Q1 expectations?
Q4 seasonality to Q1 is typical. Commercial vehicle market seems to be rebounding, with freight rates and Class 8 orders picking up from November through February.
This improvement should translate to stronger demand in H2 2026, setting up well for 2027. What is Allient supplying into this market, and how do you see it evolving?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Are you asking about commercial automotive specifically or all vehicles?
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
Yeah
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Truck and construction, or all of them?
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
All of them. I’m interested in the full picture.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
We saw improvements across commercial automotive, bus, construction, marine, agricultural, truck, rail, and Power Sports. Vehicle business remains a single-digit percentage. We define “vehicle” broadly to include all these sectors.
Vehicle markets have long design cycles, are cost competitive, and capital intensive. Investments are focused elsewhere. Power Sports has grown automotive-like. One-time Q4 impact is about $2.5 million.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
Okay.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
In Q4, across agricultural, construction, and other vehicles, we supply actuators and steering applications—gas, petrol, or electrified. We also provide electrohydraulics in larger vehicles. Expertise focuses on steering, extending to industrial applications as well.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
That helps. Thanks.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Ted. Operator, are there any more questions?
Operator
This concludes the Q&A. Returning the conference to management for closing remarks.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you for joining today. We will participate in the J.P. Morgan Industrials Conference in Washington, DC, on 17 March. Please reach out anytime. We look forward to speaking after Q1 2026 results. Have a great day—this concludes the call.
Operator
The conference is now concluded. Thank you for attending.

Craig Mychajluk
Senior Vice President of Operations
Yes. Thank you, and good morning, everyone. We certainly appreciate your time today as well as your interest in Allient. On the call today are Dick Warzala, our Chairman, President and CEO; and Jim Michaud, our Chief Financial Officer. Dick and Jim will review our third quarter 2025 results, provide a strategic and operational update and share our outlook. We will then open the line for your questions.
As a reminder, our Q3 earnings release and the accompanying slide presentation are available on our website at allient.com. If you're following along, please turn to Slide 2 for our safe harbor statement. During today's call, we may make forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those indicated. These risks and factors are outlined in our SEC filings and in our Q3 earnings release.
We also discuss certain non-GAAP measures, which we believe will be useful in evaluating our performance. You should not consider the presentation of this additional information in isolation or as a substitute for results prepared in accordance with GAAP. We have provided reconciliations of non-GAAP to comparable GAAP measures in the tables accompanying the earnings release as well as the slides.
So with that, please turn to Slide 3, and I'll turn it over to Dick to begin. Dick?
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
Thank you, Craig, and welcome, everyone. Allient delivered another strong quarter, underscored by double-digit revenue growth, record gross margin and continued deleveraging of our balance sheet. These results reflect the combination of healthy demand across key end markets and the tangible benefits of the efficiency initiatives we have put in place through our Simplify to Accelerate Now program.
On the demand side, we saw notable strength in our industrial verticals, particularly power quality solutions for data center applications as well as improving trends in automation. Our defense programs executed well and the medical market delivered steady growth even as mobility solutions remained soft. In addition, our vehicle business improved, led by contributions from commercial automotive and construction.
Profitability was another highlight with gross margin reaching a new record and operating leverage driving meaningful year-over-year improvement. Importantly, these gains were not only a result of volume, but also a reflection of mix shift toward higher-value programs and ongoing cost discipline.
Cash generation and balance sheet strength remain central to our story. Year-to-date, we have delivered significantly higher operating cash flow and further reduced debt, which has lowered our leverage ratio and enhanced financial flexibility. Jim will walk through some temporary impacts for the quarter, but at a high level, our results so far this year demonstrate our ability to convert top line performance into stronger profitability, robust cash flow and balance sheet progress.
Stepping back, Q3 was not just about the numbers. It was about discipline and execution. The results highlight the resilience of our diversified portfolio, the value of our operational transformation and our ongoing alignment with long-term secular growth drivers. Together, these elements reinforce the momentum we are building as we move toward year-end and beyond.
With that, let me turn it over to Jim for a more in-depth review of the financials.
James A. Michaud
Senior VP & Chief Financial Officer
Thank you, Dick, and good morning, everyone. Please turn to Slide 5. Q3 revenue increased $13.5 million year-over-year, reaching $138.7 million, reflecting strong industrial market demand along with solid performance in our other core end markets. Foreign exchange contributed $2.3 million in tailwinds with the remainder organic. Sequentially, revenue declined less than 1% as the second quarter included $3 million to $4 million of customer pull-ins related to anticipated supply constraints on components with heavy rare earth content. Sales to U.S. customers accounted for 57% of Q3 revenue, with Europe, Canada and Asia Pacific representing the balance.
Breaking down performance by market. Industrial market revenue advanced 20%, led by strong demand for power quality solutions in data centers as well as improving industrial automation trends, which more than offset softness in oil and gas. Medical grew 6% with surgical instruments offsetting weaker mobility solutions. Vehicle sales were up 6%, supported by commercial, automotive and construction.
Aerospace and defense revenue was up 2% as scheduled defense and space program deliveries continued. We did experience some short-term shipment delays linked to customer validations during our Dothan facility transition, but overall, demand remains intact and positions us well as validations complete. Distribution channel sales were down 6%, though they represent a smaller share of our overall mix.
Turning to Slide 6. Here, we show the composition of our revenue over the trailing 12 months, along with the year-over-year change in each market and the key drivers of that change. As you can see, our industrial market is our largest vertical at 48% of total revenue, supported by continued strength in data center applications. While industrial automation is still working through the tail end of destocking, we are seeing healthier order flow, which has helped offset softer demand in oil and gas applications.
Aerospace and defense increased to 15% of revenue, reflecting both timing of defense and space program deliveries as well as strong execution on our growth initiatives in this sector. Demand remains solid and our pipeline in defense continues to provide visibility and to sustained growth. Medical accounted for 15% of revenue led by higher demand for surgical instruments. This growth was partially offset by softness in certain pump-related products and mobility solutions. But overall, the medical sector continues to represent a steady contributor.
Vehicle represented 17% of revenue compared with 22% in the prior year. The year-over-year decline primarily reflects reduced demand in powersports and select truck applications. That said, within the quarter, we did see strength from commercial automotive helping to partially balance the softness in recreational markets. Overall, this slide reinforces that our revenue base is better aligned with higher-value, margin-accretive opportunities. We are deliberately positioning the company towards markets with strong secular growth drivers while also managing through areas experiencing softness.
Turning to Slide 7. Gross profit reached $46.2 million with gross margin expanding to a record 33.3%, up 190 basis points year-over-year and 10 basis points sequentially. This marks our fifth consecutive quarter of margin expansion. Drivers included mix improvement, higher volumes, disciplined lean -- and disciplined lean manufacturing execution.
